inventory_basis.method: Pinned git show blobs; Markdown section ranges, documented state tables/JSON keys/environment/frontmatter; AST test identities including parameterization declarations; explicit code-only source observations.

behaviors.text: Design reuse sweep, architecture fit, module placement, explicit interfaces, risks and test strategy
behaviors.reason: These design disciplines do not depend on host APIs

behaviors.text: Task contracts, dependency ordering, sizing evidence, acceptance criteria and verification instructions
behaviors.reason: Preserve the planning rules independently of task storage

behaviors.text: Reviewer personas, consensus/blind/doubt and dimension rubrics
behaviors.reason: Preserve prompt content and review criteria; registration is R05

behaviors.text: Blind reviewer receives the spec and rubric without implementation narrative
behaviors.reason: Context exclusion is a required invariant on every host

behaviors.text: Review artifact sections, verdicts, evidence, tests and finding provenance
behaviors.reason: Preserve observable review outputs and completeness rules

behaviors.text: Test-first discipline, adversarial test checks, red-check, per-task review and final verification
behaviors.reason: Preserve the pipeline's existing conditional rules and gates

behaviors.text: Finding consolidation, severity, decisions, bounded rework and severe-issue custody intent
behaviors.reason: Preserve decision policy while storage changes under R12

behaviors.text: Fast-track card schema, explicit files/constraints/tests/gates, ordered cards
behaviors.reason: Its task contract is independent of host orchestration

behaviors.text: Durable reports, audit history, attempts and explicit lifecycle cleanup
behaviors.reason: Historical evidence must survive runtime migration

behaviors.text: Mechanical review facts, style/split checks and test-quality checks
behaviors.reason: Keep deterministic algorithms and their fixtures

behaviors.text: PRD frontmatter behavior, eligibility checks and resume-by-artifact rules
behaviors.reason: Keep policy semantics; translate state and execution interfaces separately

behaviors.text: Root manifest, versioning, installation and release catalogs
behaviors.reason: Generate client metadata from one portable source of truth

behaviors.text: `run-autopilot`, status, explicit PRD, review-batch
behaviors.reason: Invoke the current phase and the local skill or OVCAQ runtime path through tested host entry points

behaviors.text: `design-solution`, PRD selection and `--rework`
behaviors.reason: Replace path/dispatch assumptions while preserving reviewed-design behavior

behaviors.text: `plan-tasks`, replanning, expansion gates and tier classification
behaviors.reason: Emit normalized task records with explicit provider-neutral tier policy

behaviors.text: 18 native agents, worker wrappers and effort choices
behaviors.reason: Retain Claude definitions in supported compatibility assets; add registration and model mappings for other hosts

behaviors.text: `work`, Tess/Devon/Ivan/Pat, checkpoints and per-task commits
behaviors.reason: Replace dispatch/wait/task-state APIs; preserve isolated roles and existing gates

behaviors.text: `review-work-completion`, reviewer fan-out, retries and close
behaviors.reason: Require independent jobs and authoritative review-gated transitions

behaviors.text: `review-blindly` standalone entry point
behaviors.reason: Replace its foreground-Claude/timeout mechanics without weakening blindness

behaviors.text: `review-plan` and its question flow
behaviors.reason: Replace host plan-mode and question-tool assumptions

behaviors.text: `fast-track`, `--push`, delta review, ledgers and bounded rework
behaviors.reason: Preserve explicit push intent and full review requirements through host/runtime contracts

behaviors.text: Code-selected full, fast-track and solo lanes
behaviors.reason: Controller extraction must preserve source lane/escalation transitions; parity is a release blocker

behaviors.text: State writer, atomic transitions, task/attempt APIs, recovery and backups
behaviors.reason: All durable workflow writes go through Autopilot's one controller; helpers prepare artifacts/proposals

behaviors.text: Loop, fresh sessions, review-once, pause/resume, limits and notifications
behaviors.reason: Use OVCAQ supervision and provider adapters

behaviors.text: Tracon fleet/task/agent views, controls and stream rendering
behaviors.reason: Map presentation to Lantern and normalized observations/controls to OVCAQ operations API

behaviors.text: Waves, worktrees, review slots, assembly, abort and landing
behaviors.reason: Preserve this capability only after its supervisor contract is established

behaviors.text: Critical custody, push refusal, stub minting and deferred follow-up
behaviors.reason: Requires both durable ownership and pre-action enforcement

behaviors.text: PRD-location hook
behaviors.reason: Retain Claude hook logic; adapt registration and editor/terminal events for additional hosts

behaviors.text: Phase-delegation and post-leave guards; departure recording
behaviors.reason: Retain Claude guards; map other hosts' events while preserving phase ownership and handoff

behaviors.text: Context cap and contract-card reinjection
behaviors.reason: Retain Claude behavior; adapt other hosts' context measurements and compaction events without changing budget policy

behaviors.text: State-write, review-completeness and live-lane Stop hooks
behaviors.reason: Retain Claude hooks; prove equivalent enforcement and feedback on each additional host

behaviors.text: Codex, Gemini and Sonnet runner commands/options
behaviors.reason: Preserve backend semantics through permission, event, quota and job adapters

behaviors.text: Runner recursion guard and host markers
behaviors.reason: Permit authorized coordinators while retaining bounded child dispatch

behaviors.text: Hook doctor check/repair, dry-run and exit meanings
behaviors.reason: Keep host-scoped operator maintenance separate from unattended execution

behaviors.text: Qwen optional lane, health checks and output guards
behaviors.reason: Keep an optional capability; absence must retain the documented fallback

behaviors.text: Legacy/shadow/workflow consensus engines
behaviors.reason: Host-local workflow execution needs an explicit adapter; preserve legacy fallback

behaviors.text: Catchup, engram context, agoge QA, rationalization synonyms and notification integrations
behaviors.reason: Declare capability dependencies and their existing failure/fallback contracts

behaviors.text: Plugin roots, reference paths and cross-skill helpers
behaviors.reason: Resolve from the installed package without Claude text substitution

behaviors.text: Python locking, process signals and OS probes
behaviors.reason: `fcntl`/process-group behavior requires a declared Unix baseline or OS adapters

behaviors.text: Anthropic connectivity probe, Claude plugin registry pins and home-directory registries
behaviors.reason: Move provider-specific runtime assumptions to their owners

behaviors.text: Release checks and test fixture locations
behaviors.reason: Separate shipped runtime from maintainer tooling without losing behavioral tests

behaviors.text: Sonnet runner does not forward the effort requested by its callers
behaviors.reason: Make the documented effort contract executable and verify generated argv

behaviors.name: prd
behaviors.text: | `prd` | string | PRD filename (with `.md` extension), e.g. `"00004-feature-x.md"`. Resolves to `docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/<prd>` while active, or `docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold/<prd>` after a Phase 2 (`oversized_task`) or Phase 6 (`escalation_exhausted`) stall move. Phase 0's `subagent_prompt_overrun` replan handler does NOT move the PRD — it replans in place (PRD stays in `wip/`); a context-cap fire rotates (also in place, no move). Written by Phase 0 step 6 at PRD selection. The dashboard derives `name` by stripping the extension. |

behaviors.name: phase
behaviors.text: | `phase` | enum | Current gate: `build`, `review`, `done`, `paused`. `build` is ONE session (selection → catchup → design → planning → work, no mid-build handoff); the review surface runs in a fresh session; blind and doubt scrutiny are lenses inside every review cycle (PRD 00015), not phases. **Legacy values** `blind`/`doubt` (pre-00015 state files) map to the review gate on resume — `resume_target.py` sends them through one full review cycle. |

behaviors.name: next_phase
behaviors.text: | `next_phase` | string | Gate the next session of `/autopilot:run-autopilot` will run. Written by `/autopilot:run-autopilot` at every transition. **Read by the `autoclaude` wrapper after each headless session exits (PRD 00014)**: a non-empty gate (`build`/`review`/`done`) → relaunch a fresh session, and `""` (empty, batch end) → archive state and stop the loop (drained). The authoritative resume signal is `phase` + `phases_completed`; build re-entry is by artifact (capsule freshness, tasks-exist, all-done). |

behaviors.name: prd_budget_since
behaviors.text: | `prd_budget_since` | string? | ISO UTC timestamp marking the start of the current PRD's `_AUTOPILOT_PRD_BUDGET_USD` spend window. Stamped by `enter.py`'s `_write_prd` (step 10) when absent, or when the pre-write state's `prd` differs from the one being selected — so a PRD re-entry after a rotation or hand-off keeps its original stamp, and a genuinely new PRD selection gets a fresh one. Read by `cli/loop_decision.py` to total metrics-ledger spend since this timestamp against the budget; a total over budget parks the PRD (`park_site: "budget"`). Cleared by Phase 9 step 10 on PRD-to-PRD reset. |

behaviors.name: loop_entry
behaviors.text: | `loop_entry` | object? | PRD 00282: the Phase 0 (`enter()`) result the loop ran in-process before launching a build session, or before consuming a `park-requested` marker — `Loop._pre_enter`. Shape: `{"entered_by": "loop", "prd": string, "result": object}`, where `result` is the same dict `autopilot enter` would otherwise print (its `warnings` key already popped and sent to the loop's own stderr). The session brief's `## Entry` section mirrors `result`'s `prd`/`catchup`/`design`/`stop`. The next `autopilot enter` call (inside the launched session) reads this FIRST: a `loop_entry.prd` matching `state.prd`, with no `--prd` given, replays `result` as that call's one JSON line and deletes `loop_entry` without re-running `enter()` — so a selection produces exactly one resume row. A `loop_entry` whose `prd` no longer matches (stale — state moved on since the loop wrote it) is dropped and `enter()` runs normally. Absent when `enter()` raised `state.StateError`, when the state write failed (one stderr line, logged, no `loop_entry`), or in a manual/interactive session (which never runs `_pre_enter`). Also cleared by Phase 9 step 10 on PRD-to-PRD reset, as defense-in-depth against a crash between the loop's write and the launched session's consume. |

behaviors.name: catchup_mode
behaviors.text: | `catchup_mode` | enum | `"run"` (default; Phase 1 honors the batch cache), `"skip"` (PRD frontmatter requested skip), `"force"` (PRD frontmatter forces full catchup ignoring the batch cache at the PRD's first entry; once `tasks` is a non-empty list the same value reads as `run`, PRD 00209), or `"skipped"` (Phase 1 was bypassed for this PRD). Set at Phase 0 from PRD frontmatter `catchup:`; defaults to `"run"` on missing/malformed frontmatter. |

behaviors.name: design_mode
behaviors.text: | `design_mode` | enum? | `"run"` (default; the Phase 1.5 design sub-step invokes `/autopilot:design-solution`), `"skip"` (PRD frontmatter requested skip), or `"skipped"` (Phase 1.5 was bypassed for this PRD). Set at Phase 0 step 4 from PRD frontmatter `design:`; defaults to `"run"` on missing/malformed frontmatter. Read by the Phase 1.5 design sub-step. Cleared by Phase 9 step 10 on PRD-to-PRD reset (re-derived from the next PRD's frontmatter at Phase 0). Absent on plans created before this field existed. |

behaviors.name: design_gate
behaviors.text: | `design_gate` | string? | `"user"` when PRD frontmatter `design_gate: user` requests an interactive review pause after design; absent otherwise. Set at Phase 0 step 4 from PRD frontmatter `design_gate:` (only an exact `user` match writes the field). Read by Phase 1.5: when `"user"`, the sub-step PAUSEs with the design doc summary via `AskUserQuestion` before planning. Cleared by Phase 9 step 10 on PRD-to-PRD reset. Absent in normal operation (no gate requested). |

behaviors.name: plan_expansion_override
behaviors.text: | `plan_expansion_override` | bool? | `true` when PRD frontmatter `plan_expansion: allow` opts the PRD out of the plan-expansion gate (`autopilot check-plan --prd`, `plan-tasks` step 5.5); absent otherwise. Set at Phase 0 step 5 by `autopilot frontmatter` (only an exact `allow` match writes the field). Read by no gate directly - `cli/policy.plan_expansion` re-reads the PRD text's frontmatter for the override; this field is the state-visible mirror. Cleared by Phase 9 step 10 on PRD-to-PRD reset (`cli/records.PER_PRD_RESET_FIELDS`). Absent in normal operation. |

behaviors.name: design_doc
behaviors.text: | `design_doc` | string? | Path to the reviewed design doc the Phase 1.5 design sub-step produced: `docs/dev/project-management/designs/<prd-stem>-design.md` (`<prd-stem>` = `prd` minus `.md`). Written by Phase 1.5 on a successful `/autopilot:design-solution` run, or set to the existing path when the artifact is reused. Read by `/autopilot:plan-tasks` (copies the doc's `## Interfaces & contracts` into task `Contract`s) and `/autopilot:review-work-completion` (appends the doc under a `## Design Doc` heading to reviewer context). The design doc FILE is a durable artifact under `docs/dev/project-management/designs/` (like review files — never deleted); only this state reference is cleared by Phase 9 step 10 on PRD-to-PRD reset. Absent on PRDs that skipped design (`design_mode == "skipped"`) and on plans created before this field existed. |

behaviors.name: phases_completed
behaviors.text: | `phases_completed` | string[] | Membership markers for finished review surfaces. Post-00015 the writer appends `"review"` at review-loop convergence (`phase-done --outcome converged`) and, since PRD 00205, at a lane-routed build's close (`phase-done --outcome lane_reviewed`, the `("build", "lane_reviewed")` row with convergence's effect, so the review-coverage hook gates the lane's review file too); legacy state files may also carry `"blind"`/`"doubt"`. |

behaviors.name: cycle
behaviors.text: | `cycle` | int | Current review-rework cycle (starts at 1) |

behaviors.name: rework_cap
behaviors.text: | `rework_cap` | int | Effective review-rework cycle cap for the current PRD. Parsed by Phase 0 from PRD frontmatter field `rework_cap: <int>`; defaults to `2` when absent, missing, or invalid. Compared against `cycle` at Phase 5 decision gate: rework allowed while `cycle < rework_cap`; pause when `cycle >= rework_cap`. Per-PRD scope, but re-derived by Phase 0 step 4 from the next PRD's frontmatter on every PRD-to-PRD transition (default 2), so it needs no explicit Phase 9 step 10 clear. |

behaviors.name: doubt_reviewer
behaviors.text: | `doubt_reviewer` | enum? | Doubt-lens roster flag for the current PRD. Parsed by Phase 0 step 4 from PRD frontmatter field `doubt_reviewer:`; accepted values `codex` (default) and `fable`; defaults to `codex` when absent, unrecognized, or on malformed frontmatter (one-line warning logged on the unrecognized-value / malformed path, none on plain absence). Read by the review phase (PRD 00015): when `fable`, Eve (Fable 5) joins the review batch as a fifth lens running the same doubt prompt as Bob, and the rubric verdicts are recorded per reviewer with `source` tags; when `codex` (or absent) the standard roster runs unchanged. Per-PRD scope, re-derived by Phase 0 step 4 from the next PRD's frontmatter on every PRD-to-PRD transition (default `codex`), so it needs no explicit Phase 9 step 10 clear. **Note (PRD 00077):** `review-work-completion`'s codex doubt-roster guard may override this field's RESOLVED value in memory for a single review dispatch (when any task attempt carries `implementor: "codex"`, the doubt leg must not be codex alone) — the guard's own rule lives in `review-work-completion`, not here. The STORED value in `state.json` is untouched by that guard; Phase 0 step 4 remains its sole writer. Absent on plans created before this field existed. |

behaviors.name: consensus_engine
behaviors.text: | `consensus_engine` | enum? | Engine behind Alice's consensus leg for the current PRD. Parsed by Phase 0 step 4 from PRD frontmatter field `consensus_engine:`; accepted values `legacy` (default), `shadow`, `workflow`; defaults to `legacy` when absent, unrecognized, or on malformed frontmatter (one-line warning on the unrecognized-value / malformed path, none on plain absence). Read by `review-work-completion` step 1: `legacy` runs today's single review subagent unchanged; `workflow` makes the `review-fanout` workflow Alice's leg (dimension fan-out, dedup, adversarial verify); `shadow` runs both, legacy gating and the workflow recorded as a non-gating observation. Per-PRD scope, re-derived by Phase 0 step 4 from the next PRD's frontmatter on every PRD-to-PRD transition (default `legacy`), so it needs no explicit Phase 9 step 10 clear. The workflow's `runId` is NOT stored here — it is stamped into the review file's `consensus_run_id` frontmatter, because `resumeFromRunId` is same-session only. |

behaviors.name: session_model
behaviors.text: | `session_model` | enum? | Model the build session launches on for the current PRD (PRD 00200). Parsed by Phase 0 step 5 from PRD frontmatter field `session_model:`; accepted values `sonnet` (default) and `opus`; defaults to `sonnet` when absent (silently) or unrecognized (one-line warning). Read by `cli/routing.build_model` as promotion signal 1 (§ Build-Session Model Promotion Signals below), which re-reads the PRD's own frontmatter rather than this mirror. `default_model` is NOT this field: it floors the per-task tier for `/autopilot:plan-tasks` and no longer picks the orchestrator. Per-PRD scope, re-derived by Phase 0 from the next PRD's frontmatter on every PRD-to-PRD transition, so it is deliberately not in `records.PER_PRD_RESET_FIELDS`. Absent on state files written before this field existed. |

behaviors.name: lane
behaviors.text: | `lane` | enum? | The effort lane `cli/lane.py` classified the current PRD into: `solo`, `fast-track` or `full`. Written by Phase 0 step 5 (the `frontmatter` verb) from the PRD text and its flat frontmatter pairs: a `lane:` override wins (`override`), else a hook path, a security-ish path, no named path or `design:` other than `skip` route to `full`, zero production paths to `solo`, a card-sized PRD to `fast-track`, the rest to `full` (PRD 00204). An invalid `lane:` value warns once and takes the classified lane; an absent key is silent. Re-derived per PRD at Phase 0, so it is NOT in `cli/records.PER_PRD_RESET_FIELDS`. Absent on plans created before this field existed. |

behaviors.name: lane_reason
behaviors.text: | `lane_reason` | string? | The first classifier rule that matched: `override`, `hook`, `security_path`, `unparsed`, `design`, `no_production_code`, `card_sized` or `uncardable`. Written beside `lane` by the same verb; rendered in the batch report's `- Lane:` line. Re-derived per PRD at Phase 0. |

behaviors.name: lane_effective
behaviors.text: | `lane_effective` | enum? | The lane that actually runs: `lane` when it is in `lane.RELEASED_LANES` (`full`, `solo` since PRD 00205, `fast-track` since PRD 00206) and `_AUTOPILOT_LANES` is not `off`, else `full` (an unreleased lane is recorded and rendered, acted on by nothing; step 5.5 prints the `running full` banner when it differs from `lane`). The fast-track runbook rewrites it to `full` with `lane_reason: "uncardable"` when `cards_from_prd.py` refuses the PRD. `_AUTOPILOT_LANES=off` in the loop environment forces `full` for every PRD; the `frontmatter` verb is that knob's one reader. Copied into every `loop-metrics.jsonl` session row and the closing `batch.completed_prds` record. Re-derived per PRD at Phase 0. |

behaviors.name: lane_escalated
behaviors.text: | `lane_escalated` | object? | `{"from": <lane>, "signal": <slug>}` when a lane-routed build escalated into the full review gate (PRD 00205). Written by `autopilot lane-check` in the same transaction that sets `lane_effective: "full"`: `unnamed_path` (a hook or production path in `work_start_sha..HEAD`), `security_diff` (`lane.security_triggered` fired), `check_failed` (a git command failed; the check fails toward the expensive lane), or a session-determined `--signal` (`critical_finding`, `high_unresolved`, `suite_red`, `review_failed`). Rendered as `, escalated from <from>: <signal>` on the report's `- Lane:` line and copied into the closing `batch.completed_prds` record. Per-PRD work product, so it IS in `cli/records.PER_PRD_RESET_FIELDS` (its lane siblings are re-derived at Phase 0 instead). Absent when no escalation happened. |

behaviors.name: tasks_total
behaviors.text: | `tasks_total` | int | Total task count. Derived from the `tasks` snapshot: every writer of `tasks` recomputes `tasks_total = len(tasks)` in the same write (the pidash-era PostToolUse sync hook is retired, PRD 00063). |

behaviors.name: tasks_completed
behaviors.text: | `tasks_completed` | int | Number of completed tasks. Derived with `tasks_total`: `tasks_completed = count(status == "completed")`, recomputed on every `tasks` write. |

behaviors.name: tasks
behaviors.text: | `tasks` | object[] | Canonical task list for the current PRD: `{"id": "<task-id>", "name": "...", "status": "pending\|in_progress\|completed", "description"?: string, "blocked_by"?: int[], "model"?: "haiku\|sonnet\|opus\|fable", "attempts"?: object[]}`. Include `id` — state readers (tracon, the review phase, `rework_task_ids` targeting) key on it. The two optional entry fields `description` and `blocked_by` are detailed in the `tasks[].description` and `tasks[].blocked_by` rows below. |

behaviors.name: tasks[].model
behaviors.text: | `tasks[].model` | enum? | Per-task model tier: `"haiku"`, `"sonnet"`, `"opus"`, `"fable"`. `"fable"` (PRD 00076) is reachable **only** via the Fable rescue gate (`references/recovery.md` § Rework escalation exhausted, on a human-approved ledger entry), never by the plan-tasks tier classifier and never as a session model. Set by plan-tasks step 4.7's tier classifier (`classify_tier.py`) and rewritten by /autopilot:run-autopilot Phase 6 escalation (see `references/phase-review.md` Phase 6). The dashboard, the review phase, and `/autopilot:work` read this field. When absent (plans created before PRD 00025), `/autopilot:work` omits `model` and subagents inherit the session model. |

behaviors.name: tasks[].attempts
behaviors.text: | `tasks[].attempts` | object[]? | Per-task execution log: `{"attempt": int, "model": string, "outcome": "completed"\|"aborted"\|"review_flagged"\|"rework_failed"\|"escalated", "review_cycle": int\|null, "cause": string\|null, "implementor": "claude"\|"gemini"\|"qwen"\|"codex"\|"orchestrator", "preflight_outcome": "healthy"\|"pi_missing"\|"endpoint_unreachable"\|"model_id_missing"\|"completion_failed"\|null, "pipeline"?: "minimal"\|"lean"\|"full", "self_deslop"?: string, "escalation_reason"?: "gate_failure"\|"review_flag"\|"fable_rescue", "escalated_from"?: "qwen"\|"haiku"\|"sonnet"\|"opus"\|"codex", "diagnosis"?: "spec_gap"\|"solid_spec", "repair_used"?: true, "breaker_skipped"?: true, "qwen_gate_failed"?: true, "qwen_excluded_reason"?: "files"\|"memory_pressure"\|"memory_probe_failed", "codex_no_edit"?: true, "codex_no_edit_probe_exit"?: int, "micro_lane"?: "overrun", "reflow"?: string, "review"?: string, "style_gate"?: string, "devon"?: "skipped:prose"\|"exploit_fixed"\|null, "devon_exploit"?: string, "devon_weak_points"?: int, "devon_in_contract"?: string[], "split_hygiene"?: string, "verification"?: string}`. Records each Work pass on the task. Appended by `/autopilot:work` at task exit (success or abort). The `implementor` field reflects what actually dispatched (NOT what step 3's routing table initially picked — a qwen pick that fell back to Claude on preflight failure records `"claude"`). The `preflight_outcome` field is set only for attempts on qwen-eligible tasks (effective eligibility after runtime write-set reconciliation); for non-qwen-eligible attempts (UI tasks, `opus`-tier tasks, backend tasks where `qwen_eligible` is `false` or absent) it is `null`. A qwen-eligible attempt that the breaker (row 3) or the memory-pressure gate (row 4) rerouted also records `null`, because the probe never ran. The `pipeline` field records the tier-gated pipeline depth the attempt ran — `"minimal"`/`"lean"`/`"full"` for `haiku`/`sonnet`/`opus`, `"full"` for `fable`, and `"solo"` for a task the solo lane's session edited itself (`references/lane-solo.md`, PRD 00205; always paired with `implementor: "orchestrator"`) (the rescue rung runs the deepest pipeline, like `opus`; absent/legacy `model` is treated as `sonnet` → `"lean"`), written at every task exit (PRD 00044) — the `?` in the signature marks read-side tolerance for pre-00044 rows only; new writes always include `pipeline`. **Cardinality (PRD 00065):** today `/autopilot:work` appends exactly one entry per task at exit. Under in-loop escalation the rule widens to one entry per rung/dispatch-group: each rung that dispatched writes its own entry when the task escalates away from it or exits on it. `attempt` numbers stay sequential across rungs (`len(existing)+1`). This is a widening, not a break — a task that never escalates still writes exactly one entry, byte-identical to today. **Six escalation fields (PRD 00065, all optional, absence = legacy / not-applicable):** `escalation_reason` (`"gate_failure"` stamped by `/autopilot:work` on the entry of the rung it escalated INTO (in-loop diagnosis); `"review_flag"` stamped by phase-review Phase 6 on its escalation path; `"fable_rescue"` (PRD 00076) stamped by the Fable rescue gate on the entry of the human-approved fable retry, always paired with `escalated_from: "opus"` and an entry `model` of `"fable"` (the rescue rung — the one tier `/autopilot:work` never selects on its own). Absent = none of the three (legacy / no escalation)); `escalated_from` (string?; normally a tier — on the entry of the rung escalated INTO, the immediate-prior rung it came from; the one exception is `"codex"` (PRD 00077), which names a BACKEND rather than a tier — stamped on the Claude entry a codex capability failure escalates into, the others are all tiers. Absent on non-escalated entries); `diagnosis` (string?; the 2nd-failure diagnosis verdict, stamped on the entry of the rung that was diagnosed); `repair_used` (bool?; `true` stamped on the entry of the same-tier attempt that ran after a task-description repair; absent otherwise, never written `false`); `breaker_skipped` (bool?; `true` stamped on a qwen-eligible attempt the breaker rerouted off qwen — to codex (PRD 00077) or to Claude at original tier (no preflight probe); absent otherwise); `qwen_gate_failed` (bool?; `true` stamped on an `implementor:"qwen"` entry whose pre-commit output guard or step-5.5 gate FAILED — the durable signal the qwen capability breaker keys on; absent otherwise). Runtime exclusions are described in the dedicated `tasks[].attempts[].qwen_excluded_reason` row below; planner metadata is unchanged. **Codex no-edit fields (PRD 00077, both optional):** `cause` gains the value `"codex_no_edit"` — the no-edit infra arm, stamped when the codex helper exited 0 with a non-empty output file but produced no working-tree change (the hook-blocked, prose-only case); classified as INFRA, so the attempt falls back to Claude at the task's own tier with no `escalation_reason` stamp. `codex_no_edit` (bool?; the LATCHED detector result, captured at the dispatch boundary — `work` SKILL.md step 4, before step 5's `git add` — by comparing the task's own file slice porcelain before and after the codex dispatch; step 5.5 reads this latched flag and never re-runs the detector. Absent on non-codex attempts and on attempts written before PRD 00077). `codex_no_edit_probe_exit` (int?; the detector's own exit code, recorded ONLY when the detector exited non-zero — a non-zero exit means the probe is INDETERMINATE, not "no change": `codex_no_edit` is NOT latched and the attempt continues on the capability path normally. Exists so a broken detector is visible in the record instead of silently reclassifying every real codex capability failure as infra. Absent when the detector ran cleanly and on attempts written before PRD 00077). The `"escalated"` outcome value is stamped on the entry for a rung the task was reset away from and escalated up; the final rung's entry carries the real terminal outcome (`completed`/`aborted`), and the escalated-away entry keeps its true `implementor` (a qwen rung escalated to Sonnet keeps `implementor:"qwen"`; likewise, a codex attempt records `model` at the task's own tier, e.g. `"sonnet"`, with `implementor: "codex"` carrying the backend identity — the same split the qwen rung already uses). **Micro-lane fields (PRD 00148, both optional):** `implementor` gains `"orchestrator"` — the one value meaning no implementor dispatched at all, stamped when a small rework task was edited in-session by the orchestrator (`work/references/rework-mode.md` § Micro lane), which also records `red_check: "n/a:micro-lane"`. `micro_lane` (string?; `"overrun"` when the lane's post-edit ceiling fired, the edit was reverted and the task fell through to a normal dispatch — that attempt records the real dispatcher in `implementor`; absent otherwise). `reflow` (string?; `"<path>:<hunks>"`, `;`-joined for several, when `/autopilot:work` step 5's `check_reflow.py` flagged a staged file, or `"failed:<stderr>"` when the script could not run; absent when nothing was flagged). **Per-task review field (PRD 00159):** `review` (string?; `"failed:<cause>"` when the step-5.7 reviewer lane failed twice, `"failed:invalid_output"` when both replies broke the reporting contract and `parse_review.py` rejected each, `"skipped:test-only"` when every path in `<task_base_sha>..HEAD` was test or fixture code outside rework mode; may also carry a `medium-retry:fixed`/`medium-retry:unfixed` suffix from PRD 00140. Absent when the review ran cleanly or the haiku tier-gate skipped it). **Per-task style gate (PRD 00163):** `style_gate` (string?; the step-5.65 verdict on that task's own diff — `"clean"`, `"fixed:<sha>"` (one fix dispatch landed and the re-run was clean), `"failed:<detail>"` (the violation lines joined by `"; "`, or the script's stderr when the gate could not run), or `"skipped:tier"` for a `haiku` task. Absent on attempts written before PRD 00163, when the gate ran once per phase and stamped nothing per task). **Devon weak-point fields:** `devon` gains the value `"exploit_fixed"` — stamped when step 2.9's Devon broke the tests, Tess strengthened them once, and the task proceeded on the strengthened tests with no second Devon dispatch. `devon_exploit` (string?; Devon's one-line weak-point summary, stamped alongside `devon: "exploit_fixed"`; absent otherwise). `devon_weak_points` (int?; the count of weak points Devon's numbered `Weak points:` list named, stamped alongside `devon: "exploit_fixed"`; absent otherwise). `devon_in_contract` (string[]?; each `"N. in-contract: ..."` line Tess returned when answering Devon's weak points, stamped alongside `devon: "exploit_fixed"`; absent otherwise). **Per-task split-hygiene check (PRD 00166):** `split_hygiene` (string?; the step-5.65 verdict on the test files that task touched — `"clean"`, `"fixed:<sha>"` (one deletion-only fix dispatch landed and the re-run was clean), `"failed:<detail>"` (the reported lines joined by `"; "`, or the script's stderr when the check could not run), or `"skipped:no-tests"` when the task's candidate list held no test path. Distinct from `style_gate` because the two answer different questions on different file sets: one measures line spans over every `.py` file, the other reads bindings in test files only. Absent on attempts written before PRD 00166 and when the haiku tier-gate skipped step 5.65). **Verification stamp (PRD 00167):** `verification` (string?; `"skipped:<cause>"` when step 5.5's per-task test verification could not run at all, or `"timeout:<command>"` when step 5.5's narrow tests hit their 300000 ms Bash `timeout` budget and then hit the 600000 ms re-run too, leaving no verdict, per `work/references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Foreground command budgets. `<command>` names the command that timed out. Two neighbouring timeouts are never stamped here: a step-2.95 red-check takes `red_check: "skipped:<cause>"` from its own ladder, and a step-7 timeout is recorded in the phase report, that suite running after every attempt entry has been appended. Absent when the task's tests ran). See `work/references/attempt-logging.md` for field semantics, the atomic write procedure, and the attribution row-ownership table. Outcome upgraded later by /autopilot:run-autopilot Phase 6: `review_flagged` at the start of escalation (step 2), then `rework_failed` if the chain exhausts at `opus` (or at `fable`, when a rescue attempt was spent — step 3's escalation-exhausted branch). Rework reads the last entry's `model` to determine the next tier. Absent on plans created before PRD 00025; `implementor`/`preflight_outcome` absent on attempts written before PRD 00031; `self_deslop` absent on attempts written before PRD 00041; `pipeline` absent on attempts written before PRD 00044; the six escalation fields and the `"escalated"` outcome value absent on attempts written before PRD 00065; the attempt-level `qwen_excluded_reason` absent on attempts written before PRD 00075; `codex_no_edit` and `codex_no_edit_probe_exit` absent on attempts written before PRD 00077. |

behaviors.name: tasks[].attempts[].cause
behaviors.text: | `tasks[].attempts[].cause` | string? | Qwen pre-commit output causes: `"qwen_no_edit"` (no task-owned implementation diff) and `"qwen_test_mutation"` (Tess-owned tests differ from the test commit). Both record a rejected Qwen row with `outcome: "escalated"`, `qwen_gate_failed: true`; the new Sonnet row carries `escalation_reason: "gate_failure"`, `escalated_from: "qwen"`. Existing abort causes are unchanged; successful attempts use null. |

behaviors.name: tasks[].attempts[].qwen_excluded_reason
behaviors.text: | `tasks[].attempts[].qwen_excluded_reason` | string? | Runtime exclusion: `"files"` for zero or stale multi-file `FILE_PATHS`, `"memory_pressure"` or `"memory_probe_failed"` for row 4. A write-set exclusion records `preflight_outcome: null` and preserves the plan-time task fields. Absent when no runtime exclusion fired. |

behaviors.name: tasks[].attempts[].self_deslop
behaviors.text: | `tasks[].attempts[].self_deslop` | string? | Outcome of the per-task self-deslop pass that `/autopilot:work` runs as step 5.6 between test-pass (5.5) and per-task code review (5.7). Allowed values: `"committed:{sha}"` (the self-deslop subagent committed a `chore: prune slop from ...` cleanup), `"noop"` (subagent ran but found no slop, no commit), `"skipped:trivial"` (skip rule fired — diff added <30 net lines OR touched <2 files), `"skipped:test-only"` (PRD 00159; every path in `<task_base_sha>..HEAD` is test or fixture code, checked before the trivial rule), `"timeout"` (subagent watchdog killed it), `"errored:{cause}"` (dispatch failed; `{cause}` is a short tag). Optional; absent on legacy attempts (pre-PRD-00041) and on attempts the writer never updated. Self-deslop is best-effort: it never blocks a task, never triggers retries, and never modifies the `outcome` field. The per-task review at step 5.7 runs against the post-cleanup diff when a cleanup committed; against the original diff otherwise. |

behaviors.name: tasks[].estimated_tokens
behaviors.text: | `tasks[].estimated_tokens` | int? | Per-task input-token budget estimate. Set by plan-tasks step 4.7's tier classifier; persisted directly in `state.tasks[]`. Absent when plan-tasks did not record a budget estimate. |

behaviors.name: tasks[].est_context_peak
behaviors.text: | `tasks[].est_context_peak` | int? | Per-task estimated peak working-context size. Used to predict subagent dispatch budget headroom. Set by plan-tasks step 4.7's tier classifier; persisted directly in `state.tasks[]`. Absent when plan-tasks did not record a context estimate. |

behaviors.name: tasks[].qwen_eligible
behaviors.text: | `tasks[].qwen_eligible` | bool? | Qwen routing eligibility (PRD 00174): backend (not UI) AND tier ∈ {`haiku`, `sonnet`} AND exactly one non-empty expected implementor-writable file AND no public-contract edit. Empty or missing file slices are ineligible. Set by plan-tasks step 4.7's tier classifier; persisted directly in `state.tasks[]`. `/autopilot:work` reconciles this flag against concrete `FILE_PATHS` before routing, without rewriting the plan; absent (legacy plans) is treated as `false`. |

behaviors.name: tasks[].qwen_excluded_reason
behaviors.text: | `tasks[].qwen_excluded_reason` | string? | Why plan-tasks step 4.7 excluded the task from qwen routing: `"ui"`, `"tier"`, `"contract"`, or `"files"` (first failing condition in that order; `files` includes zero and two-or-more writable files). Set by plan-tasks step 4.7's tier classifier on every ineligible task (PRD 00019); persisted directly in `state.tasks[]`. Absent on eligible tasks and legacy plans — the Phase 9 Implementor Mix render counts an ineligible task with no reason as `unknown`, never an error. |

behaviors.name: tasks[].tier_reason
behaviors.text: | `tasks[].tier_reason` | string? | Why the planner assigned the task its tier **at plan time**. Legal values: `"test_port"` (every path in the task's slice is a test path, pinned to `sonnet`), `"packaging"` (every path is a test or packaging path, pinned to `sonnet`), `"contract"` (the task itself edits a public contract, so `opus`), `"algorithmic_risk"` (the task's own Details name a new algorithm, shared mutable state, or a migration, so `opus`), `"mechanical"` (the haiku row), `"default"` (the `sonnet` fallback), and `"floor"` (the PRD frontmatter `default_model` floor raised the classified tier). Written once by `/autopilot:plan-tasks` step 4.7 from `classify_tier.py`'s output; persisted directly in `state.tasks[]` and **never rewritten afterwards**: a later escalation rewrites `model` only, and `attempts[]` carries that history, so `model: "opus"` with `tier_reason: "mechanical"` is an escalated task, not a corrupt record. No reason maps to `fable` (see the `tasks[].model` row). Absent on plans created before PRD 00160. |

behaviors.name: tasks[].description
behaviors.text: | `tasks[].description` | string? | Free-form detail about what the task must achieve, beyond the one-line `name`. Validated by `cli/schema.py`: optional, and when present must be a `str` (any other type — including `bool` — is rejected as `tasks[<i>].description`). Absent on tasks that carry only a `name`. |

behaviors.name: tasks[].blocked_by
behaviors.text: | `tasks[].blocked_by` | int[]? | Integer references to the tasks this one waits on. Validated by `cli/schema.py`: optional, and when present must be a `list` whose every element is a plain `int` — `bool` elements are rejected, matching the bool-is-not-int rule the int fields already use. An empty list is valid. Absent on tasks with no dependencies. |

behaviors.name: tasks[].carry_refs
behaviors.text: | `tasks[].carry_refs` | string[]? | Upper-cased `Ref` cells of every consolidated-findings row that re-queued THIS task as `[C{cycle}]`, unioned across every cycle that re-flagged it (`references/phase-review.md` Phase 6 step 4 and `references/recovery.md` § Rework escalation exhausted's Fable rescue gate both write it via `task-set-meta`). `autopilot review-close` (`cli/review_close.py` `_carry_unmatched`) is the sole reader: a `carry`-classified findings row is accepted only when its `ref`, upper-cased, appears here with the matching `carry_cycle`. Absent on a task never re-queued by a review flag. |

behaviors.name: tasks[].carry_cycle
behaviors.text: | `tasks[].carry_cycle` | int? | The review cycle whose `carry_refs` union is current — set alongside `carry_refs` on every write, always `state.cycle` at write time. `autopilot review-close` requires `carry_cycle == state.cycle` in addition to the ref match (a stale cycle's union does not back a later cycle's carry row). Absent on a task never re-queued by a review flag. |

behaviors.name: task_aborts
behaviors.text: | `task_aborts` | object[] | Per-task abort log: `{"task_id": string, "turn": int, "total_input_tokens": int, "cause": "subagent_prompt_overrun"}`. One writer: `/autopilot:work` Subagent Dispatch Budget appends a `cause: "subagent_prompt_overrun"` entry when an assembled subagent prompt exceeds 50K after one trim pass. (The context cap no longer writes here — it ROTATES, appending to `cap_rotations`.) Sets `turn: -1` when the actual turn is unknown (the assembly carries no turn counter). Empty array on fresh state. **`task_aborts[]` is ephemeral per-PRD state — Phase 9 step 10 clears it on PRD completion.** |

behaviors.name: cap_rotations
behaviors.text: | `cap_rotations` | object[]? | Context-cap rotation log: `{"task_id": string, "cycle": int, "phase": "build"\|"review"}` (`phase` since PRD 00196; entries written before it carry none and were all build rotations). Appended by `autopilot_context_cap_hook.py` when a Work turn during `build`, or during review-phase rework (`rework_task_ids` non-empty), exceeds the hard usage cap (`USAGE_CAP`, 500K) or the 450-call tripwire — a ROTATION, not a replan: the hook also sets `next_phase` to the phase it left and resets the in-flight task's status from `in_progress` to `pending` (so the fresh session's `/autopilot:work`, which iterates pending tasks, re-attempts it as the first non-completed task; a review session resumes at Phase 6 via Phase 4's third skip). The Stop hook then writes the `next` signal on STOP (the model writes no signal). Apart from the one in-flight task's `status`, leaves `tasks`, `phases_completed`, and `replan_count` untouched; writes no `stall_reason` and no `replan-context.md`. **Livelock guard:** if the last entry already names the in-flight task in the same phase, a second consecutive fire on the same task sets `stall_reason.stalled == "oversized_task"` (and `next_phase` to that phase) instead of appending another rotation (one oversized task costs at most two rotations before a loud stall); a build-era entry never counts against the task's fresh attempt in review. Ephemeral per-PRD state — Phase 9 step 10 clears it. Absent on fresh state and on plans created before this field existed. |

behaviors.name: replan_count
behaviors.text: | `replan_count` | int? | Number of replans applied to the current PRD after Phase 0 saw a `subagent_prompt_overrun` stall (the one surviving replan trigger; a context-cap fire rotates instead and leaves `replan_count` unchanged). Incremented by Phase 0's replan procedure before each retry. Each replan tightens the per-task budget by halving (floored at 40K) — see `recovery.md` "Budget floor guard" for the `target_budget = max(40000, int(75000 / (2 ** (replan_count - 1))))` schedule. Phase 0 PAUSEs only when `replan_count > 5` AND the same task keeps aborting (genuinely execution-overflowing, not capability-bound). Reset to 0 by Phase 9 step 10 when the PRD completes. Absent or 0 means the current PRD has not been replanned. |

behaviors.name: work_start_sha
behaviors.text: | `work_start_sha` | string? | Git `HEAD` SHA captured at Phase 3 start, immediately before `/autopilot:work` is dispatched. Bounds the commit range `work_start_sha..HEAD` produced by this PRD's `/autopilot:work` dispatches — read by Phase 8 to scope the codex doubt review's diff (`<work_start_sha>..HEAD`). Captured once per PRD; in a multi-PRD batch each PRD overwrites it with current HEAD at Phase 3 start, so ranges never overlap. **Empty-tree fallback (PRD 00084):** when `git rev-parse HEAD` fails at capture (unborn branch / no commits yet), this is set to the git empty-tree sentinel `4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904` so the review range spans the whole tree instead of being undefined (core `SKILL.md` § Phase 3 invariants). Cleared by Phase 9 step 10 on PRD-to-PRD reset. Optional: absent on plans created before this field was introduced, and on PRDs where Phase 3 has not yet run. |

behaviors.name: repo_root
behaviors.text: | `repo_root` | string? | Absolute path to the git repo containing the work commits (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`), captured at Phase 3 start alongside `work_start_sha`. Usually equals the project root; differs when the work repo is nested under a non-git project root (e.g. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot` under `~/.claude`). Read by the review session to run `git` (diff gathering, `head_sha` capture) in the right repo. Cleared by Phase 9 step 10 on PRD-to-PRD reset. Optional: absent on older plans; consumers fall back to the project root. |

behaviors.name: git_dir
behaviors.text: | `git_dir` | string? | The `--git-dir` value the Phase 3 "Capture `repo_root`" step had to pass for a bare-repo-backed project root (`~/.buvis` → `/Users/<you>/.buvis`), captured at Phase 3 start alongside `repo_root`; left unset when a plain `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` worked. Read by the cap_critical custody capture (`cli/custody.git_argv`, which builds `git --git-dir <git_dir> --work-tree <repo_root>`) and by `autopilot custody resolve`. Cleared by Phase 9 step 10 on the PRD-to-PRD reset (`records.PER_PRD_RESET_FIELDS`, right after `repo_root`). Absent on plans created before this field existed and on plain-repo projects. |

behaviors.name: rework_task_ids
behaviors.text: | `rework_task_ids` | string[]? | Set by `/autopilot:run-autopilot` Phase 6 (rework) to instruct `/autopilot:work` to process only those task IDs at their escalated tier. Non-empty puts `/autopilot:work` in rework mode (skip completed-not-flagged tasks; re-iterate the listed IDs). Cleared (set to `[]`) by `/autopilot:run-autopilot` after the rework `/autopilot:work` pass finishes. Empty/absent means full-plan dispatch — the default Phase 3 behavior. A non-empty list beside this cycle's review file on disk means rework queued, dispatch pending: Phase 6 hands off after task-add in loop mode and the next session resumes the dispatch (PRD 00208). |

behaviors.name: qwen_gate_failures_consecutive
behaviors.text: | `qwen_gate_failures_consecutive` | int? | Consecutive qwen capability failures (pre-commit output rejection or step-5.5 gate failure), counted among qwen attempts ONLY (PRD 00065) — a non-qwen task (Claude/Gemini) between two qwen failures leaves it UNCHANGED (neither reset nor incremented). Only a qwen gate PASS resets it to 0; batch rollover also resets it. Incremented per qwen gate failure. Latches the breaker at 2. Owned entirely by `/autopilot:work`. Legacy state lacking the field: readers treat it as 0. |

behaviors.name: qwen_breaker
behaviors.text: | `qwen_breaker` | object? | Qwen capability breaker state (PRD 00065): `{"tripped": bool, "after_task": "<task-id>"\|null, "failed_tasks": ["<id>", ...], "batch_id": "<batch.id>"}`. `tripped:true` once the counter reaches 2. `after_task` = the task id whose failure tripped it; `failed_tasks` = the two consecutive failing ids; `batch_id` = the batch this breaker state belongs to. Batch-scoped: `/autopilot:work` resets the breaker lazily when `qwen_breaker.batch_id != state.batch.id` (fallback id `"no-batch"` for a manual `/autopilot:work` run with no `state.batch`). Once tripped, stays tripped for the rest of the batch. Legacy state lacking the field: readers treat it as `{tripped:false}`. |

behaviors.name: codex_probe
behaviors.text: | `codex_probe` | object? | Batch-scoped codex health probe result (PRD 00077): `{"batch_id": "<state.batch.id>"\|"no-batch", "verdict": "healthy"\|"unhealthy", "backend": "codex"\|"copilot", "detail": "<one-line cause>"\|null, "checked_at": "<ISO 8601>", "hook_doctor?": "ok"\|"stale: <basenames>"\|"<doctor summary line>"\|"doctor error: <config path>"}`. Written once per batch by the codex batch health probe (`work` SKILL.md § Batch codex health probe) and read by the step-3 routing interception before any codex dispatch. Batch-scoped with the same LAZY reset `qwen_breaker` uses: `/autopilot:work` re-probes and overwrites the slice when `codex_probe.batch_id != state.batch.id` (fallback id `"no-batch"` for a manual run with no `state.batch`); a match reuses the cached verdict and never re-probes. Writers MAY carry additional descriptive keys beyond these five (the live probe also stamps `model` and `note`); readers ignore unknown keys. Absent on legacy state files: readers treat absence as "not yet probed", never an error. **`hook_doctor`** (optional): the doctor-first sub-probe's own verdict (`work/references/codex-implementor.md` § Codex batch health probe), from `codex_hook_doctor.py check` run before the live probe. `"ok"` when the doctor exits 0; `"stale: <basenames>"` when it exits 3 (the stale/no_canonical targets' basenames). On doctor exit 1 or 2 the live probe is skipped entirely and `verdict` is forced `"unhealthy"`, but the two exits document DIFFERENT `detail`/`hook_doctor` shapes because the doctor's own output differs on each path: on **exit 1** (a broken target exists) `hook_doctor` carries the doctor's own summary line (`"<n> ok, <n> stale, <n> broken"`) and `detail` carries `"hook_doctor: <the first broken TSV line>"`; on **exit 2** (the doctor itself could not run: the config is missing, unreadable, not JSON, or has no `hooks` object; an event entry is malformed; a command does not tokenize; the plugin manifest has no `aegis@buvis-plugins` entry; or a target I/O call failed. On this path it emits neither a TSV line nor a summary line, only a single `error: <reason>` line to stderr that names the cause) `hook_doctor` carries `"doctor error: <config path>"` and `detail` carries `"hook_doctor: <the doctor's stderr error line>"`. Absent on state files written before the doctor-first probe existed. |

behaviors.name: qwen_preflight
behaviors.text: | `qwen_preflight` | object? | Batch-scoped qwen preflight probe result (PRD 00093), mirroring `codex_probe`'s shape and idiom: `{"batch_id": "<state.batch.id>"\|"no-batch", "verdict": "healthy"\|"pi_missing"\|"endpoint_unreachable"\|"model_id_missing"\|"completion_failed", "detail": "<the failing check's own detail string>"\|null, "checked_at": "<ISO 8601>"}`. `verdict` reuses the four existing `preflight_outcome` strings directly — no separate `"unhealthy"` wrapper. Written once per batch by `work` SKILL.md § Qwen infra preflight (step 3 routing row 5) and read there before every qwen-eligible dispatch. Batch-scoped with the same LAZY reset `codex_probe`/`qwen_breaker` use: `/autopilot:work` re-probes and overwrites the slice when `qwen_preflight.batch_id != state.batch.id` (fallback id `"no-batch"`); a match reuses the cached verdict and never re-probes. **Re-probe trigger is scoped to backend-health signals, not task-outcome signals** — an ordinary step-5.5 gate failure on a qwen attempt does NOT invalidate the cache (that is the one-shot-to-Sonnet escalation's job); only a Subagent Watchdog hang/lost-result on the qwen dispatch itself, or an infra-shaped exit from `qwen-run.sh` at real dispatch time despite a cached `"healthy"` verdict, deletes the field via `statectl del qwen_preflight`, so the next qwen-eligible task's batch-scope check re-probes. Absent on legacy state files: readers treat absence as "not yet probed", never an error. |

behaviors.name: stall_reason
behaviors.text: | `stall_reason` | object? | Signals a pending recovery action. Three shapes: `{"stalled": "oversized_task", "task": "<id>", ...}` (written by `/autopilot:plan-tasks` when a task can't be split below budget — carries `estimated_tokens?: int`; AND by `autopilot_context_cap_hook.py`'s livelock guard on a second consecutive cap fire for the same in-flight task — carries `total_input_tokens: int`; both trigger a stall move to `docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold/`); `{"stalled": "subagent_prompt_overrun", "task": "<id>", "prompt_bytes": int}` (written by `/autopilot:work` Subagent Dispatch Budget when an assembled subagent prompt exceeds 50K after one trim pass — triggers Phase 0's **replan procedure**, not a stall move; see `replan_count` and `/autopilot:run-autopilot` Phase 0 "Handle Work-phase abort"); `{"stalled": "escalation_exhausted", "task": "<id>"}` (written by `/autopilot:run-autopilot` Phase 6 when a task at tier `opus` fails rework — Phase 6 performs its own stall move inline); `{"stalled": "taskcreate_failed", "detail": "<error>"}` (written by `/autopilot:plan-tasks` step 4 when a `task-add` call fails mid-plan, after it rolls back the tasks it already created — PRD 00084; the `taskcreate_failed` value is a retained legacy key name, not a live tool reference; Phase 2 folds any non-`oversized_task` stall into its `plan_tasks_fail` PAUSE / loop re-invoke-once path, and `/autopilot:plan-tasks` clears this marker itself on a successful retry). **Merged** (not replacing) into state by the writer, then **cleared** by `/autopilot:run-autopilot`. Lifecycle handoff: Phase 2 handles `oversized_task` inline with a stall move; Phase 0 of the next session handles `subagent_prompt_overrun` via the replan procedure (no stall move — the PRD stays in `wip/`, planning re-runs with `replan-context.md`); Phase 6 handles `escalation_exhausted` inline (it owns the rework path and does its own move + clear before signaling — Phase 0 should never see this in normal operation, and treats it as crash recovery if it does). The context cap no longer writes `stall_reason` on a normal overrun — it ROTATES (see `cap_rotations`); only its livelock guard escalates to `oversized_task`. Absent in normal operation. |

behaviors.name: cap_pause_reason
behaviors.text: | `cap_pause_reason` | object? | Set by Phase 5 when the rework cap is hit AND the current review did not converge (`cycle >= rework_cap` AND unresolved findings remain). A clean cycle-at-cap convergence does NOT trigger cap-pause — it falls through to Phase 7 hand-off. Records the unresolved review findings and the cycle count. Shape: `{"cycle": int, "cap": int, "unresolved_findings": object[]}`. **Distinct from `stall_reason`'s `oversized_task`, `subagent_prompt_overrun`, and `escalation_exhausted` shapes** — `cap_pause_reason` is a separate top-level state field, not another `stall_reason` discriminator. The authoritative, durable indicator of a cap pause is `phase == "paused"` PLUS this field — not `needs_attention`. Cleared by (a) the Phase 0 Cap-Pause Resume Handler on user "resume", (b) Phase 9 step 10's PRD-to-PRD reset, and (c) the per-PRD reset lists in `recovery.md`. Previously only (a) applied — a cap pause halts the flow before Phase 9, so Phase 9 step 10 never observed this field in normal operation — but (b) and (c) are now added as defense-in-depth against the residual-leakage path (a manual "abandon" followed by a manual PRD move, which falls outside the automated flow). Absent in normal operation. |

behaviors.name: pause_reason
behaviors.text: | `pause_reason` | object? | Set by every turn-ending PAUSE row alongside `phase == "paused"` / `next_phase == "paused"`. Shape: `{"site": string, "detail": string}`. `site` is a stable slug, one of: `"sub_skill_fail"`, `"reviewer_fail"`, `"plan_tasks_fail"`, `"mv_verify"`, `"batch_end"`, `"replan_exhausted"`, `"work_incomplete"`, `"systemic_park"`, `"statectl_fail"`. **`statectl_fail`** (PRD 00084; flow revised by PRD 00051 task 9) names a `statectl` state-write that failed twice (lock contention, python error, unreadable state). The model no longer hand-edits `state.json` to record it: after retry + `autopilot restore` the failure is signaled via the `state-write-failed` marker (§ Marker files) and the turn ends — the wrapper halts on the marker without needing a `pause_reason` write. The slug remains in this enum for states written by older sessions and for the loop-mode stall record that uses the same site. **`systemic_park`** (PRD 00066) is written by the Phase 0 park handler when `batch.parks_consecutive` reaches 2 (sanctioned-halt row 9). **Converted out of this enum by PRD 00066:** `blocking_escalation` and `scope_alarm` no longer write `pause_reason` — in loop mode a blocking escalation runs the Loop-mode stall procedure (deferred-JSON `type:"stall"`, `site:"blocking_escalation"`) and a scope alarm defers-and-continues; interactively both remain mid-turn `AskUserQuestion` prompts. `clarification` likewise pauses no batch: a Phase 2 ambiguity is assumed through, or stalls (`site:"clarification"`) under `pause_on_ambiguity: true`. `detail` is a one-line human-readable string; free-form, not parsed by any consumer. **Lifecycle invariant: `pause_reason` is present ONLY during an unresolved pause.** Cleared by (a) the pre-Phase-0 `### Resuming` session-start cleanup, unconditionally, on EVERY resume; (b) the Phase 9 step 10 PRD-to-PRD reset; and (c) every per-PRD reset list in `recovery.md`. NOT overwritten by normal phase progression — this is the difference from `phase` (which advances on every transition), and the reason the explicit clears above exist. Cap-pause keeps its own `cap_pause_reason` marker and does NOT write `pause_reason`. Read by the CLI loop's decision table (`cli/loop.py`; a pause marker stops the loop and surfaces `detail` in the notification). Absent on fresh state and whenever no pause is active. |

behaviors.name: review_cycles
behaviors.text: | `review_cycles` | object[] | History of each review cycle. Each entry: `{"cycle": int, "review_file": "<path>", "agents": {"alice": "...", "bob": "...", "carl": "...", "diana": "..."}, "issues_found": int, "follow_up_tasks": int, "deferred": int, "recurring_issues": string[]}`. Cycles 3+ may also carry `decision_gate`, `rework_commits`, `rework_notes`, `cycle3_fix_audit`, `test_run` written by user-override paths (see live state for examples). |

behaviors.name: review_cycles[].recurring_issues
behaviors.text: | `review_cycles[].recurring_issues` | string[] | Issue descriptions that appeared in a previous cycle |

behaviors.name: review_lenses
behaviors.text: | `review_lenses` | object? | Live lens roster for the CURRENT review cycle, stamped by `review-work-completion` step 5 at dispatch and closed out in step 6: maps lens -> `"running"\|"done"\|"failed"\|"lost"\|"skipped"`. `"lost"`: the persona had an open dispatch row and no line at all under that cycle's `agents:` frontmatter block — nothing was ever reported back (`cli/review_close.py` `_lens_states`'s missing-persona fail-safe). `"skipped"`: the persona was taken off the roster on purpose, `agents:` status `"disabled"` (`_LENS_STATUS`). Keys: `consensus` (Alice), `blind` (Blake), `doubt` (Bob), plus `ui` (Carl), `fable` (Eve) when active. REPLACED at each cycle's dispatch; tracon expands the review phase strip from it. Absent on standalone runs and pre-field state files. |

behaviors.name: autonomous_decisions
behaviors.text: | `autonomous_decisions` | object[] | Decisions made without user input, one batch-report row per entry. Two entry shapes. An ORDINARY decision needs all five of: `cycle` (plain `int`; `bool` is rejected, matching the bool-is-not-int rule the int fields use; no floor, ceiling, or roster of known cycles), `severity` (one of the five strings published as `cli/schema.py::DECISION_SEVERITIES`: `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, `n/a`, matched exactly, so case and whitespace variants are rejected), and three prose pairs each satisfied by a non-empty `str` under EITHER spelling: `issue`\|`question`, `action`\|`disposition`, `reason`\|`resolution` (vocabularies may be mixed across pairs). An `assumed-ambiguity` decision (`type == "assumed-ambiguity"`, that exact value) is judged by its own two keys instead, non-empty `question` and `assumption`, and carries no cycle, severity, action or reason. Extra keys are always allowed, including the optional `research` field for research-backed decisions, and including `assumption` or a `type` of any other value on an ordinary entry. Enforced by `cli/schema.py::validate_changed` on the entries a write ADDS, counted by OCCURRENCE, not by membership (a write adds an entry whenever it pushes the number of copies of that value past the number the pre-write list held; each copy the pre-write list already held is matched off by value (never by key names, key count, `type` or position) and carries over unjudged, so a reorder and a removal add nothing, and only the copies past that count are judged, wherever in the list they sit), never by `validate()`: entries an older batch left behind are never re-judged, so a resumed state still loads. A refused entry raises the single message shape `autonomous_decisions entry missing <key>`, naming the FIRST key of the pair (`issue`, not `question`), for absent, blank, wrong-typed and out-of-enum values alike; `statectl` prints it as `rejected: ...` with exit 1 before `state.json` is touched. |

behaviors.name: deferred_decisions
behaviors.text: | `deferred_decisions` | object[] | Decisions requiring user input. May include optional `research` field when research was attempted but inconclusive. |

behaviors.name: doubts
behaviors.text: | `doubts` | object[] | LEGACY (pre-00015 Phase 8): findings from the standalone doubt review, `{"description": "...", "category": "fix\|verify\|known", "justification?": "...", "status": "pending\|resolved", "source?": "codex\|fable"}`. Post-00015 the doubt lens's findings enter the normal review consolidation instead, so no new entries are written; Phase 9 step 6 still collects any lingering pending entries from old state files. Empty array on fresh state. |

behaviors.name: doubts_rubric_verdicts
behaviors.text: | `doubts_rubric_verdicts` | object[]? | Per-rule verdict block recorded by the review phase's consolidation (PRD 00015; `review-work-completion` SKILL.md step 6) from the doubt lens's `D{n}: pass\|fail` lines — Bob's (codex or his Claude fallback), plus Eve's when she ran. Each entry: `{"rule_id": "D{n}", "verdict": "pass"\|"fail", "source?": "codex"\|"fable"}`. **Id prefix (PRD 00108):** the doubt set is `D1-D5`; state written before that rename carries the old `R`-prefixed ids and is read as-is — nothing rewrites historical state. **`source?`** (PRD 00038, optional): written only when both doubt-lens reviewers ran (one entry per rule per reviewer, 10 entries); the single-reviewer path keeps 5 entries with no `source`. REPLACED every review cycle; the final cycle's verdicts are the durable ones. Used by Phase 9 step 7 to populate the "Doubt Rubric Verdicts" section of the batch report (see `references/batch-report-format.md`). Cleared by Phase 9 step 10 on PRD-to-PRD reset (per-PRD scope). Absent on PRDs that have not yet run a review cycle and on state files written before this field existed. |

behaviors.name: needs_attention
behaviors.text: | `needs_attention` | bool | Dashboard flag. Sole remaining writer: Phase 5 cap-pause MAY set `true` as a best-effort dashboard hint (the pidash Notification/PostToolUse hooks that set and cleared it are retired, PRD 00063). Nothing clears it automatically now — treat it as advisory only; tracon (PRD 00062) will own the read/clear lifecycle. **Dashboard-only state — NOT the authoritative cap-pause signal.** The authoritative cap-pause signal is `phase == "paused"` plus `cap_pause_reason` being set.

behaviors.name: contract_card
behaviors.text: | `contract_card` | string? | Compact re-anchor card (PRD 00087 R1): current step, active invariants, next gate. Written by `/autopilot:run-autopilot`, `/autopilot:work`, and `/autopilot:review-work-completion` at each gate transition (via `statectl set`, in the same write that advances `phase`/`next_phase`). Read by the `reinject_contract_card.py` SessionStart(compact) hook, which re-injects it after a within-session compaction. Interactive runs use a scratch `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/contract-card.md` instead. Absent until the first gate transition writes it. Free-form; not parsed by any consumer. |

behaviors.name: phase_guard
behaviors.text: | `phase_guard` | object? | RETIRED (PRD 00014, with `autopilot_stop_hook.py`). May linger in pre-00014 state files; ignored by all consumers. |

behaviors.name: thrash_halt
behaviors.text: | `thrash_halt` | object? | RETIRED (PRD 00014, with `autopilot_stop_hook.py`). May linger in pre-00014 state files; ignored by all consumers. |

behaviors.name: batch
behaviors.text: | `batch` | object? | Tracks completed PRDs across sessions |

behaviors.name: batch.id
behaviors.text: | `batch.id` | string | Batch ID: `yyyymmddHHMM` timestamp of first execution |

behaviors.name: batch.mode
behaviors.text: | `batch.mode` | string | Always `"autopilot"` |

behaviors.name: batch.unavailable_reviewers
behaviors.text: | `batch.unavailable_reviewers` | string[]? | Reviewers permanently rejected this batch, currently `["carl"]`. Absent means `[]`. Review step 5 appends once only when `gemini-run.sh` exits 4; step 1 reads before any binary probe and suppresses dispatch/retry and the `ui` lens. Preserved in full across per-PRD reset with `batch`; removed with the batch so the next batch retries Carl. When interactive batch end retains `state.json`, Phase 0's closed-batch identity rollover explicitly deletes this field and `batch.unavailable_reviewer_details` alongside the new id. An operator may remove Carl's entry and paired detail at a session boundary after repair. |

behaviors.name: batch.unavailable_reviewer_details
behaviors.text: | `batch.unavailable_reviewer_details` | object? | First-failure provenance paired with `unavailable_reviewers`: `{"carl": {"cycle": 1, "prd": "00175-example.md"}}`. Review step 5 writes it alongside the list in the same merge, never overwriting an existing origin. Step 6 uses these original values for `carl: skipped (permanently unavailable since cycle {n} of {prd})` in every subsequent review; missing legacy origin renders `unknown`. Same batch lifetime as the list; sibling entries are preserved. |

behaviors.name: batch.parks_consecutive
behaviors.text: | `batch.parks_consecutive` | int? | Consecutive `wrapper_died` parks (Phase 0 park handler) with NO healthy PRD outcome between them — the systemic-park breaker (PRD 00066). Lives under `batch` so it survives the per-PRD reset. Incremented by 1 in the park handler's per-PRD-reset write; at `>= 2` the handler PAUSEs the batch (`pause_reason.site = "systemic_park"`, sanctioned-halt row 9). Reset to 0 on ANY healthy outcome — Phase 9 PRD completion, and any non-`wrapper_died` Loop-mode stall (the stall procedure resets it whenever `site != "wrapper_died"`, `references/recovery.md`). Default 0; legacy state lacking the field: readers treat it as 0. |

behaviors.name: batch.completed_prds
behaviors.text: | `batch.completed_prds` | object[] | PRDs finished so far: `{"filename", "cycles", "autonomous_decisions", "escalated_decisions", "tasks_completed", "tasks_total"}`. Appended by `statectl.py`'s `complete-prd <prd-filename>` verb, which computes the entry from the state being closed (`cycles` = `cycle`; `autonomous_decisions` = count of `autonomous_decisions` entries the batch report's "Autonomous Decisions" table renders - dicts whose `type` is not `"assumed-ambiguity"` and whose Issue cell holds text (the first non-empty string among issue / question / finding / decision / supersedes / detail), per `render_report.is_autonomous_row`; `escalated_decisions` = count of `deferred_decisions` entries whose `status` is neither `"pending"` nor `"deferred"`, mirroring `render_report._is_pending`'s exclusion rule exactly; `tasks_completed`/`tasks_total` copied as-is) and resets `batch.parks_consecutive` to 0 in the same write. |

behaviors.name: batch.skips
behaviors.text: | `batch.skips` | object[]? | PRDs the eligibility gate skipped this batch (PRD 00137): `{"prd", "command", "exit_code", "note", "at"}` per skip. Appended by `autopilot select` (`cli/__main__.py::_run_select`) whenever a `backlog` candidate's `eligibility:` frontmatter command does not exit 0 — the PRD stays in `backlog/`, gets no session, and is never parked, so a later drain re-evaluates it. `exit_code` is the command's own, or `-1` when it never ran (`note` then says `"timeout"` or `"error: <msg>"`; `note` is `""` otherwise). `at` is ISO 8601 UTC to the second. Lives under `batch` so the per-PRD reset preserves it (`records.PER_PRD_RESET_FIELDS` never touches `batch`) — the skips describe the drain, not whichever PRD it eventually picked. The FIRST pick of a fresh batch runs before `state.json` exists, so `select` can only print those records; Phase 0 step 3 seeds the field from the printed `skipped` list. Rendered by `render_report.batch_summary` as the `PRDs skipped: N` line and the `### Skipped` table. Absent until something is skipped; readers treat absence as `[]`. |

behaviors.name: batch.catchup_completed_at
behaviors.text: | `batch.catchup_completed_at` | string? | ISO 8601 UTC timestamp recorded when the most recent full `/git-ferry:catchup` invocation in this batch completed. Read by Phase 1 "Batch cache check": if present, < 4h old, AND `batch.catchup_head_sha` matches current HEAD or every commit since it has committer `autopilot-loop/<batch.id>` (loop-only movement), Phase 1 runs a delta refresh instead of full catchup. A first-entry `catchup: force` skips the 4h freshness check and reads delta iff a `catchup_head_sha` is recorded and every commit since it is loop-only. Written by Phase 1 after full catchup completes. Preserved by Phase 9 step 10 across PRD-to-PRD state resets so subsequent PRDs in the same batch can reuse the cache. Absent on first PRD of a batch and on plans that never ran full catchup. |

behaviors.name: batch.catchup_head_sha
behaviors.text: | `batch.catchup_head_sha` | string? | Git HEAD SHA captured at the moment full `/git-ferry:catchup` completed in this batch. Paired with `catchup_completed_at` for the Phase 1 cache check: a delta refresh needs current HEAD to equal this SHA, OR every commit since it to have committer `autopilot-loop/<batch.id>` — either satisfies the match, not exact equality alone. Written and preserved on the same lifecycle as `catchup_completed_at`. |

behaviors.name: catchup_probe
behaviors.text: | `catchup_probe` | object? | `{"batch_id": <string>, "gh": "ok"\|"unauthenticated"\|"absent", "engram": "ok"\|"unregistered"\|"absent", "checked_at": <ISO UTC>}` — written by `autopilot catchup-probe`, once per `batch.id`; a stale `batch_id` (different from the current batch) means the next call reprobes. Not reset by the per-PRD reset (`cli/records.PER_PRD_RESET_FIELDS` does not list it) — it is batch-scoped, like `batch.catchup_head_sha`. |

behaviors.name: batch.plugin_versions
behaviors.text: | `batch.plugin_versions` | object? | Enforcement-plugin version pin (PRD 00086 R3): `{"aegis@buvis-plugins": "<v>", "warden@buvis-plugins": "<v>"}`, recorded at batch selection (Phase 0 step 3) from `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json`. The loop's plugin-pin preflight (`plugin_drift` in `cli/loop.py`, since PRD 00106) compares it against the currently-installed versions before each session launch and halts the batch loud on any drift (never runs on enforcement code that auto-updated mid-batch — sanctioned-halt row 11). Preserved across the per-PRD reset (lives under `batch`); a genuine batch-identity rollover re-pins from the current install. Absent on pre-R3 batches → the preflight no-ops (an unpinned batch is never blocked). |

behaviors.name: batch.critical_on_master
behaviors.text: | `batch.critical_on_master` | object[]? | Display-only mirror of the `critical-on-master` marker entries, one element per pending cap_critical custody in the marker-entry shape below (§ Marker files); upserted by `do_stall`'s cap_critical single commit (`custody.mirror_mutator`, composed into the same write as the per-PRD reset) and the entry removed by `autopilot custody resolve` step 5. The marker and the journal are the sources of truth, so a stale mirror cannot block resolution (resolve prints `mirror stale, custody closed` and exits 9 when the state write fails, custody already closed). Lives under `batch` so the per-PRD reset preserves it; absent until the first cap_critical stall of a batch. |

behaviors.name: batch.minted_stubs
behaviors.text: | `batch.minted_stubs` | string[]? | Basenames of the hold triage stubs `autopilot mint-stubs --batch <batch.id>` minted for this batch (PRD 00195), e.g. `["00203-triage-partition-conflicts-missing-ddb-guard-v1.md"]`, appended (deduplicated, in mint order) by `cli/__main__.py::_run_mint_stubs` after each successful mint whenever `state.json` exists. The verb runs at three sites - after a successful `cap_critical` stall (`references/phase-review.md` § Cap check), after Phase 9 step 6's deferred migration, and at the loop-mode batch end (`references/phase-done.md`) - and each call's stdout lists only what THAT call minted, usually nothing after the first; this field is the batch-wide accumulation, so the batch-end notification's `{s} stubs` is `len(batch.minted_stubs)` rather than the final call's count. Lives under `batch` so the per-PRD reset preserves it; absent until the first mint of a batch (readers treat absence as `[]`); the stubs themselves are the durable record (`hold/<NNNNN>-triage-<slug>-v1.md`, `ledger_key` in their frontmatter), so a stale or missing field can only misreport the count, never re-mint. |

behaviors.name: pause-requested
behaviors.text: | `pause-requested` | operator (`touch`, or tracon's `p` key) | wrapper, at the next session boundary — stops the loop, notifies "paused by operator" | empty |

behaviors.name: paused-by-operator
behaviors.text: | `paused-by-operator` | wrapper, on that pause exit (`pause.stamp_paused`) | the loop itself, cleared past the pause branch on the next run (`pause.clear_paused`) — no session ever reads it | empty; its **mtime** is the stop time tracon renders |

behaviors.name: park-requested
behaviors.text: | `park-requested` | wrapper `park)` case (single writer) | Phase 0 "Handle park request" (FIRST abort-handler check); deletes it AFTER the verified `hold/` move | one-line JSON `{"prd": "<state.prd basename>", "reason": "<one-line death/thrash cause>"}` |

behaviors.name: state-write-failed
behaviors.text: | `state-write-failed` | the session (`SKILL.md` § State Management statectl-failure flow), or `autopilot_context_cap_hook.py`'s broken-boundary branches (`cli/` unimportable, or the state transaction raising) | wrapper's decision-table branch 0 (`SKILL.md` § Session Loop); HALTS the loop and does NOT delete it | one-line JSON `{"site": "statectl_fail", "detail": "<raw error>"}` |

behaviors.name: .turn-counts.json
behaviors.text: | `.turn-counts.json` | `autopilot_context_cap_hook.py`, on every qualifying PostToolUse fire | the hook itself (the per-session tripwire counter) and the build gate's gate-edge headroom check (`references/phase-build.md` Phase 1.5, PRD 00200), which reads `last` | JSON `{"counts": {"<session id>": <int>}, "fired": ["<session id>", ...], "last": {"session": "<session id>", "count": <int>, "usage": <int>\|null}}`; `last` is this session's tool-call count and context total at the hook's latest fire (`usage` is null until the transcript carries a usage line), rewritten even on the fires a leftover `.cap-fired` marker de-duplicates, so it always names the running session. Not consumed: rewritten on each fire |

behaviors.name: critical-on-master
behaviors.text: | `critical-on-master` | written by `do_stall` step 4b (`cli/custody.record_critical`, under `marker_lock`; the entry is upserted by `op_id`, so a retried stall replaces rather than duplicates it) | read by `hooks/guard_push_on_critical.py` (denies a Bash `git push` into the repo while an entry is pending) and by Phase 0 "Handle pending custody" (lists entries via `autopilot custody list`, resolves them via `autopilot custody resolve`); the file is deleted when the last entry resolves | JSON `{"entries": [ {"prd", "batch", "op_id", "commit_range", "commits", "detail", "repo_root", "git_dir", "branch"}, ... ]}`. The marker is tracked work-management state; `ledger/custody.jsonl` (§ Custody journal below) is the restore source when the marker is removed, and `custody.pending()` reads marker ∪ journal |

behaviors.name: wave.json
behaviors.text: | `wave.json` | written by `autopilot wave plan` (`cli/wave.plan`) and rewritten by `autopilot wave launch` and `autopilot wave abort` as each lane is stamped (`cli/wave_launch.py`), and by `autopilot wave assemble`, `review` and `land` (`cli/wave_assemble.py`, `cli/wave_review.py`) as the wave moves through assembly, review and landing; every writer holds an exclusive flock on the sibling `wave.json.lock` and replaces the file atomically | read by the other `autopilot wave` verbs and by nothing else — no session, gate file or hook reads it; `abort` leaves it in place with `status: "aborted"` (or `"abort_failed"`), which is what makes a later `wave plan` refuse to replace a half-cleaned wave | JSON `{"id", "status", "repo", "base_branch", "base_sha", "review_slots", "created_at", "assembly": {"worktree", "branch", "head_sha", "merged", "kept"}, "lanes": [ {"name", "order", "branch", "worktree", "prds", "paths", "status", "pid", "started_at", "worktree_created", "abort_error"}, ... ], "held_back": [ {"prd", "reason"}, ... ]}`; `status` is one of `planned`, `running`, `aborted`, `abort_failed`, `assembled`, `conflict`, `checks_failed`, `unfinished`, `done`, `assembled_partial`, `converged`, `review_failed`, `interrupted` (`cli/wave.WAVE_STATUSES`; a lane's own `status` takes every value but `done`, `converged`, `review_failed` and `interrupted`, which are wave-only), and `pid` is also the lane loop's process-group id. Disposable at wave end with `wave-slots/` (`SKILL.md` § Retention); the verbs are in `references/waves.md` |

behaviors.name: review-paths
behaviors.text: | `review-paths` | `autopilot wave review` (`cli/wave_review.review()`) | the nested autopilot loop's `gather-context.sh` path-scoping filter | one repo-relative path per line, from `review_paths(wave)`; removed together with the assembly worktree when the wave lands (`_land_cleanup`'s `git worktree remove`) |

behaviors.name: task_qwen_excluded_reason

behaviors.text: | `attempt` | object | The `tasks[i].attempts[j]` object verbatim (`tasks[].attempts` above), nothing added or normalized. |

behaviors.name: build_models

behaviors.name: attempt_tiers

behaviors.name: cycles
behaviors.text: | `cycles` | object[] | One entry per cycle `n` in `1..state.cycle`, read from `docs/dev/project-management/reviews/<prd stem>-review-<n>.md` or its zero-padded twin `-review-<nn>.md`; a missing or unparseable file yields `null` in the three sub-keys below (never zeros: absence must not read as clean). |

behaviors.name: cycles[].cycle
behaviors.text: | `cycles[].cycle` | int | `n`. |

behaviors.name: cycles[].reviewers
